content: Health indicators in Uganda, as a developing country, are significantly below global averages. Recent data indicates that the life expectancy at birth in Uganda is approximately 49 years. The child mortality rate, defined as the number of deaths before the age of five, is alarmingly high, with 140 deaths per 1,000 live births. In 2002, the total health expenditure in Uganda accounted for 7.4% of the country’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP). Uganda experienced a severe impact from the HIV/AIDS epidemic that swept through East Africa. During the early 1990s, the prevalence of HIV among Ugandan residents was 13%. However, by the end of 2003, this figure had decreased significantly to 4.1%, representing one of the most successful national responses to the AIDS epidemic in Africa. In 2003, the Ugandan Ministry of Public Health reported a cholera outbreak in the Bundibugyo district. The majority of cases were concentrated along the Semliki and Lamia rivers, highlighting the geographical spread of the disease. Uganda is also home to the Uganda Virus Research Institute (UVRI), which is recognized as one of the most advanced facilities for viral research in East Africa.
